items.title: 의뢰 맡깁니다
items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

items.content: 🚨 CVE-2026-58496 📢 Source: GitHub_M 💣 CVSS Score: 0.0 (NA) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: False Thor Vector Graphics (ThorVG) is a production-ready vector graphics engine. Prior to 1.0.7, the `SFNT/TTF` font loader's `SfntLoader::gen` function in `tvgSfntLoader.cpp` reads `data[0] through data[3]` to identify the font type without first checking that the input buffer contains at least four bytes. Loading an undersized font directly from memory through public APIs such as `tvg::Text::load` causes an out-of-bounds read. Loading through a file path using `mmap` can mask the read because of page alignment; the memory-loading API directly exposes it. Depending on memory layout, a malformed short font may crash the consuming application or disclose adjacent heap memory. This issue is fixed in version 1.0.7. 📅 Published Date: 2026-10-27T22:18:34.301Z https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-58496
items.title_ko: ThorVG 1.0.7 이전 버전의 SFNT 폰트 로더 범위 밖 읽기 취약점 CVE-2026-58496
items.summary_ko: ThorVG 1.0.7 이전 버전의 SFNT/TTF 폰트 로더는 입력 버퍼가 최소 4바이트인지 확인하지 않고 data[0]부터 data[3]까지 읽는다. tvg::Text::load 같은 메모리 로딩 API로 너무 짧은 폰트를 불러오면 범위 밖 읽기가 발생해, 애플리케이션이 충돌하거나 인접한 힙 메모리가 노출될 수 있다. 이 문제는 1.0.7에서 수정되었으며, 입력 정보에는 CVSS 점수 0.0(NA), 원격 악용 불가(False)로 표기되어 있다.
items.content_ko: ThorVG는 제품 수준의 벡터 그래픽 엔진이다. 1.0.7 이전 버전에서는 SfntLoader::gen 함수가 폰트 타입을 식별하기 위해 입력 버퍼의 처음 4바이트를 확인하지만, 버퍼 길이를 먼저 검사하지 않는다. 그래서 크기가 작은 폰트를 메모리에서 직접 불러오면 범위 밖 읽기가 발생한다. 파일 경로로 mmap을 사용해 불러오면 페이지 정렬 때문에 이 문제가 가려질 수 있지만, 메모리 로딩 API에서는 그대로 드러난다. 메모리 배치에 따라 잘못된 짧은 폰트로 소비 애플리케이션이 충돌하거나 인접한 힙 메모리 내용이 노출될 수 있다. 이 문제는 1.0.7에서 수정되었다.

items.title: Compile-Time Dependent Types
items.summary: ml, plt
items.content:
It seems inevitable that compile-time dependent types will come to systems programming.

C++ has templates and constexpr . Rust has const generics. Zig has comptime . Even C has _Generic .

However, these features tend to be highly restricted, lack a proper type system, or both.

I’m working on Syl , a language which aims to encode compile-time computation in a modal type system.

Syl is primarily inspired by András Kovács’ work on two-level type theory , as well as plans for OxCaml .

The Syl compiler may be found on GitHub .

In Syl, all values have a mode along with a type.

Modes describe properties of values independent of their types.

For example, OxCaml uses modes to indicate whether a value is uniquely owned, may be written to, may be sent to another thread, etc. 1

Syl has two mode axes: staticity and erasure .

On the staticity axis, a value may be either static or dynamic .

For example, literals are static unerased , since they are clearly knowable at both compile time and runtime.

You can check by writing a mode annotation:

Each mode axis has a sub-moding relation.

If you have a static value, it’s safe to forget that it is knowable at compile time and hence treat it as dynamic .

Similarly, an unerased value may be treated as erased .

Mode annotations may “weaken” the mode, but not “strengthen” it:

As you might expect, branching on a dynamic value causes the result to be dynamic .

As long as they don’t capture or branch on dynamic values, functions preserve staticity. 2

Functions that return erased values are themselves erased , so cannot be applied at runtime.

Now, what can we do with this information?

When a value is knowable at compile time, surrounding code can be monomorphized .

Functions of static parameters take advantage of this fact:

Whenever we call f x , the compiler requires that both f and x have mode static .

If they do, it selects a particular implementation of f specialized to the value of x .

Concretely, f true would call a function that hard-codes print_bool true , and likewise for f false .

In this example, we’re printing the value of x at runtime, so it needs to be unerased .

That’s often unnecessary: if x only determines how to compile the body of f , it can be erased .

Here, erased also implies static , so f will be specialized on x .

The if erased expression accepts a static erased condition and is guaranteed to resolve at compile time.

Therefore, the body of f true is simply print_int 0 , and likewise for f false .

On their own, the static and erased modes let us explicitly request specialization-based optimizations,

but they don’t give us dependent types. Functions of static arguments do.

Here, if erased allows us to return an integer if x is true and a boolean otherwise.

Hence, f has a dependent function type, which encodes how the result type depends on the value of the input.

Note ty as name gives the argument a name for use in the result.

Applications can then determine the correct result type by evaluating f ’s type.

There is no distinct type grammar: type formers like -> and type annotations are normal expressions.

int  and  bool are just erased values of type type , and abstracting over them gives us polymorphism.

As we saw above, functions of static arguments are monomorphized.

At runtime, id int refers to an identity function that directly operates on integers, and likewise for id bool .

That is, Syl is dependently typed at compile time and simply typed at runtime. 3

Constructs that determine the shape of the runtime program require static information.

Types are always erased , so the runtime program cannot inspect types.

Syl implements dependent typechecking similarly to existing languages, so we won’t discuss it in detail.

However, the relationship between types and propositions in Syl differs from that of languages like Lean, Rocq, and Agda.

items.title: AI and social media bans won't make California kids safer online. It may even be harmful
items.content:
Gillian Hayes is a professor and computer scientist at the UC Irvine where she co-directs the CERES Center for Children and the Digital World.

For more than two decades, my research group has been studying and supporting young people with disabilities, as they create and use digital technologies.

In one study of Autcraft , a Minecraft server built for autistic kids, a 13-year-old boy described a rich social life there that included friends he trusted, builds he led, other kids he comforted when they were struggling.

And yet, when describing this rich social life, he asked, “Will I always be not social?”

This quote has stayed with me. This sweet, social child was measuring his life against a definition of “social” that was not built for him. And the way his parents, schoolteachers and other well-meaning adults were using that definition made him feel terrible about his own experiences and the things that made him happy.

Californians are right to worry about kids online. We are right to demand of our lawmakers, teachers, administrators and tech companies responsibility for what we are all collectively bringing into the world. The lawsuits behind this year’s chatbot bills involve real children who were harmed.

Somehow, though, we keep behaving as though there is only a binary choice to either ban technologies, whether phones or AI, or keep the status quo. Both options fail the kids who need support the most.

Access bans sound protective, but the evidence so far mostly suggests they are not.

Australia’s under-16 social media ban, evaluated after three months by both the government’s own regulator and a peer-reviewed medical journal study , found more than 80% of kids still using restricted platforms. They fake their ages, borrow logins and find ways around the ban.

Worse, even when bans do reduce usage, evidence indicates they don’t actually improve things we care about, like mental health and academic performance.

What concerns me most is the possibility that we are now undoing the decades we have spent destigmatizing the use of a variety of assistive technologies and participation in online communities.

We know that many kids go online because these are some of the few communities in which they truly feel comfortable, like the 13-year-old who used Autcraft as his primary social space. Research consistently shows LGBTQ youth find identity support and community online that isn’t always available at home or school.

items.title: It was never about software alone, was it?
items.content:
I've been quiet about LLMs in general, as I have always thought that the topic is complex and touches a lot of different aspects of work, society, business, and even society. I find it difficult to grasp everything at once. And that makes it difficult to form an opinion. There are smarter people than me that can present their views in a much better way ( the Clojure Conj video of Stuart Halloway comes to mind).

I will not attempt to digest the bigger picture today, but instead focus on something smaller, specifically LLMs and software (which is a big item already). Having read so many opinions in Clojure slack channels and tech blogs I am interested in, it seems that the world of software engineers is quickly dividing itself into 2 distinct groups, those that loathe LLMs (for many good reasons), and those that either like using LLMs or pragmatically use them because they have to. I'm pretty sure there is a lot more diversification but that gets lost in the loudest voices, I guess.

Disclaimer: I do not consider myself an experienced software developer, especially since I have had many different roles on my professional career, software development only being a part of that. I've learned to program when shared UNIX workstations were still a thing. I have worked in technology since my first job some than 3 decades ago. I've been part of large research programs, worked on large technology projects for the largest Dutch Telecom provider, went into startups more than 15 years ago and have been exposed to all kinds of technologies during those years.

I've been part of teams building large scale platforms (hundreds of servers running simultaneously), have worked on client software in different forms and shapes and have had responsibility for commercialising that tech. The tech we created has always run commercially in production environments. While I do not assume I know everything there is to know about software development, I've been around it enough to understand and appreciate its complexity.

When we (my team and I) first heard about LLMs being used in software development, we were quite sceptic. Perhaps not out of a feeling of superiority, but more because we had worked hard to get a decent process in which a team with both experienced and unexperienced developers can think about new ideas, flesh them out, create working code for it and deliver it to a production environment together.

We did not quite believe an LLM interface would help us to become a better team or deliver better results. Since there was strong indication that more companies were using these models, we felt we should at least familiarise ourselves with it.

We started using them (in the wrong way) initially, by asking it questions. We didn't trust it to touch our code base, so the logical next thing was to use it as a tool like how we used search, stack overflow etc. This turned out to be a mistake. The results weren't great, and the way the LLM would deliver information did not give us a feeling of trust.

As time went on, we read about how teams were using LLMs, with things like harnesses, rules and other things to get the machine under control. That did not help much either. At some point however we had experimented a bit with code reviews (by copy-pasting some code into the prompt), and that seemed a more interesting use. We decided to add Claude as a review tool to our CI process. A developer writes code, reviews and tests himself, then pushes the branch to git, and Claude does another review when the PR is opened. And to be fair, Claude review found a lot of small inconsistencies and issues in our code that the individual developer missed. Only when there were no issues reported would we then proceed to the next step where a colleague would review the code.

This is, still, by far the most useful application for us. As models got better, their suggestions to fix issues became smarter and better. Which helps to feel a little more at ease using this…

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

items.title: Miasma Worm Targets AI Coding Agents: 73 Microsoft Azure Repos Disabled
items.content:
An unprecedented supply chain attack bypasses registry-level scanners entirely, turning developer tools including Claude Code, Cursor, and Gemini CLI into execution vectors.

The Incident: On June 3, 2026, a highly sophisticated variant of the Miasma worm (also known as Mini Shai-Hulud) launched a coordinated, two-pronged attack targeting both the npm registry and developer source code repositories.

The Escalation: The attack successfully breached multiple high-profile GitHub accounts, including the official Microsoft Azure durabletask repository, using stolen Personal Access Tokens (PATs) and backdated commits to evade traditional audit trails.

The Response: In an ultra-rapid defensive maneuver, GitHub’s automated mitigation systems disabled 73 compromised repositories – including 49 directly associated with Microsoft, Azure, and Azure-Samples within a mere 105-second window .

The Vector: Instead of relying on traditional package installation hooks, Miasma targets the developer’s local environment. It abuses legitimate auto-run, hook, and rule engines within modern IDEs and AI coding assistants ( VS Code, Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI ) to execute a malicious 4.3 MB staged dropper upon folder-open or agent initialization.

The Impact: Once detonated, the Bun-based worm harvests credentials for AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, npm, and GitHub, and automatically propagates by committing itself back into any repository the victim’s stolen tokens can write to.

At exactly 16:00 UTC on June 3, 2026, a silent, automated purge swept across GitHub. In a high-speed containment action lasting just 105 seconds, 73 active repositories vanished from the platform. Among them were 49 critical repositories belonging to Microsoft, Azure, and Azure-Samples.

This drastic mitigation followed alarming telemetry indicating that threat actors behind the Miasma malware family had regained write access to key cloud repositories. The compromise exploited a stolen Personal Access Token (PAT) belonging to an active Microsoft contributor.

While security firms like StepSecurity and JFrog scrambled to document an concurrent attack vector on the npm registry where 57 malicious packages were published, a second, far more insidious arm of the campaign was already silently spreading directly inside GitHub source repositories.

By bypassing registries and package managers entirely, the Miasma worm targeted the very tools developers use to write code. It didn’t wait for npm install . Instead, it waited for the developer to simply open their code editor or launch an AI coding assistant.

The genius of the Miasma repository-poisoning campaign lies in its exploit surface. When an attacker successfully pushed malicious commits to targeted codebases (such as the popular library icflorescu/mantine-datatable ), the commits added no actual code dependencies.

Instead, the attacker checked in five innocent-looking workspace configuration files and one obfuscated JavaScript file: .github/setup.js .

│ └── settings . json < - - Claude Code SessionStart Hook

│ └── setup . mdc < - - Cursor Agent Prompt Injection

│ └── settings . json < - - Gemini CLI SessionStart Hook

│ └── tasks . json < - - VS Code Automatic Folder - Open Task

├── package . json < -- Hijacked NPM Test Script

└── setup . js < - - The 4.3 MB Staged Dropper

Each of these configuration files is designed to abuse a legitimate, developer-friendly auto-run feature within popular modern tools. Opening the cloned directory in any of these environments instantly triggers execution.

Claude Code & Gemini CLI (SessionStart Hooks)

Both Anthropic’s Claude Code and Google’s Gemini CLI support custom hooks triggered when an AI agent initializes a session in a project workspace. items.content:
Dario Amodei, the CEO of Anthropic, in Bengaluru, India, on 16 February 2026. Photograph: Priyanshu Singh/Reuters

Dario Amodei, the CEO of Anthropic, in Bengaluru, India, on 16 February 2026. Photograph: Priyanshu Singh/Reuters

Anthropic files for potentially record-breaking stock market valuation in key test for AI industry

Market debut of firm behind Claude chatbot will be one of largest in US history, a test of AI boom’s financial viability

Anthropic has publicly filed for a stock market listing in what is slated to be one of the largest debuts in history. The company’s float on the US market will serve as a test of the financial viability of the multitrillion-dollar AI boom.

Analysts and investors have valued the San Francisco-based company, founded in 2021, at more than $1.5tn. The company, which will will list under the symbol ANT, confidentially filed with US financial regulators for an initial public offering in June.

“We believe AI is one of the most consequential technologies in human history,” the company’s investor prospectus reads. Anthropic researchers and executives have trumpeted the transformative power of AI while simultaneously warning of its potential to cause human extinction.

Anthropic researchers say AI could cause human extinction by 2030

A leader in the race to create powerful artificial intelligence models and a bellwether of the American AI boom, Anthropic’s chatbot Claude is its flagship product, which offers text generation features as well as advanced coding and cybersecurity capabilities. CEO Dario Amodei founded the company after quitting OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT.

Anthropic’s audited filings will offer the first public glimpse of its financial health, which have been the object of intense speculation in recent months as questions of a potential AI bubble swirl .

The company detailed rapidly rising revenue in the prospectus: $41m in 2023, $386m in 2024, $4.585bn in 2025 (an increase of more than 1,000%), then $16.286bn in the first six months of 2026 alone. The company disclosed that, as of the end of June, it had raised $141.1bn.

Despite the increasing revenue, Anthropic disclosed a net loss of $80bn for the first half of 2026.

Anthropic has focused on businesses as its primary paying customers, unlike OpenAI, which has courted everyday consumers for ChatGPT. As of 30 September, Anthropic said it had more than 14,000 enterprise customers – 11,900 of which had $100,000 or more of revenue, more than 1,900 that had $1m or more revenue and about 250 enterprise customers that had $10m or more revenue.

“The speed and depth of our enterprise customer adoption are powerful evidence of Claude’s position at the frontier of AI,” Anthropic executives wrote.

The filing contains some of the hyperbolic language characteristic of AI companies predicting the miraculous potential of their technology. Describing the potential of AI agents, semi-autonomous chatbots that can carry out tasks on behalf of users, Anthropic executives wrote: “The result is something without historical precedent: what we refer to as a country of geniuses in a datacenter, available to every organization and sector of the economy.”

Investing in Anthropic and the development of a model that the company claims could revolutionize knowledge work across industries comes with a great deal of risk. Anthropic listed more than 90 pages of potential to its business. For one, a “substantial portion” of the company’s revenue comes from a limited number of customers, and losing any of them could put a huge dent in their revenue. A quarter of Anthropic’s revenue comes from its top five customers, though no single customer represents more than 10% of its business.

The company also has incurred $6.2bn in debt as it built out its infrastructure and spends billions yearly on computing power provided by third parties, according to the filing.

items.title: Amazon Is Gutting Its AI Division After Sustained Failure
items.content:
By now, you’d be hard pressed to find anyone who isn’t broadly familiar with the AI heavyweights and their flagship models. OpenAI has ChatGPT, Anthropic has Claude, Google has Gemini. But what does Amazon have?

Not a whole lot, it turns out. Unlike its competitors in the tech megacorp scene, Amazon’s standout AI model — organized under the name “Nova” — is about the farthest thing from a household name. And that’s not likely to change anytime soon, because the ecommerce giant is now gutting its in-house AI labs, Bloomberg reports .

Per the outlet, Amazon is scaling back the ambitions of most of its Nova AI models and reorganizing its AI development teams as part of an effort to narrow its focus on “highest priority” goals, after its power-hungry large language models turned out to be a bust.

Accordingly, the company has put most of its AI models on ice, Amazon insiders told Bloomberg . This includes its text-based Nova models, as well as video- and image-generating models, all of which have been placed in a state of “keep the lights on,” meaning they’re technically still supported, but only receive the bare minimum resources needed to sustain them.

Instead, labor and computing power are being diverted toward a singular “frontier-model effort” led by Pieter Abbeel, director of the Berkeley Robot Learning Lab whose robotics company Covariant was hoovered up by Amazon in 2024. At the time Abbeel joined the tech giant, Covariant’s founders were working on AI models for robots, which lines up pretty well with Amazon’s push to automate everything it possibly can.

News of the shift in Amazon’s strategic focus comes a week after it closed one of its key AI offices in San Francisco, an 80-person site specializing in research on artificial general intelligence, the supposed next-level of AI development where the tech obtains human-level intelligence and reasoning skills.

With urgent questions swirling over whether LLMs can ever usher in a return on investment — let alone AGI — it may be that Amazon is jumping out of the AI hype cycle while it still can.

items.summary_ko: 작성자는 Fil-C로 컴파일한 프로그램 대부분이 수정 없이 동작하는 호환성에 감탄하고 있습니다. 작성자의 목표는 관리하는 서버들을 Fil-C로 컴파일한 코드로 바꿔 보호하는 것이며, Filian은 Fil-C를 내려받아 빌드·설치하고 Debian 소스 패키지를 Fil-C로 다시 빌드하도록 돕는 도구로 소개됩니다. 약 9,000개의 암호 소프트웨어 마이크로벤치마크에서 Fil-C 코드는 보통 clang 대비 1~4배의 사이클을 사용했습니다.
items.content_ko: 작성자는 많은 라이브러리와 애플리케이션이 Fil-C에서 수정 없이 동작하며, 예외도 해결하기 어렵지 않았다고 말합니다. 작성자의 목표는 관리하는 여러 머신을 Fil-C로 컴파일한 코드로 전환해 보호하는 것입니다. Zen 4에서 암호 소프트웨어를 대상으로 약 9,000개의 마이크로벤치마크를 clang과 비교한 결과, Fil-C 코드는 보통 clang 컴파일 코드의 1~4배 사이클을 사용했습니다. Filian은 Fil-C를 내려받아 컴파일·설치하고, 선택한 Debian 소스 패키지를 Fil-C 버전으로 빌드하도록 돕는 도구입니다. 원문에는 Debian 12 비특권 사용자 환경에서 약 10GB의 디스크 공간으로 Fil-C를 빌드하고 Fil-C로 컴파일한 NetHack을 실행하는 절차도 나오며, 다른 패키지 관리자 지원 여부와 사전 빌드된 Fil-C 바이너리 제공 여부에 대한 질문도 함께 다룹니다. 원문이 단편적으로 끊겨 있어 일부 내용은 확인되지 않습니다.

Update 5: Instagram is now leaking recovery email and phone numbers linked to an account.

Seems like every day a new security issue crops up at Instagram.

Instagram Exposing Linked Email and Phone Number

Update 4: A new report suggests that Instagram accounts may be vulnerable to coordinated mass-report abuse. According to the claim, when a newly created account is routed through a Los Angeles-based VPN and then submits a specific mix of reports in scam and fraud category, the targeted account can allegedly be banned without any human review.

Instagram Account Banning by AI by Reporting Scam and Fraud (Source: X/Twitter)

Update 3: Meta’s apparent fix for the AI bot vulnerability is difficult to take seriously. Instead of fully disabling the risky functionality, they reportedly removed it from the visible interface while leaving the underlying API endpoint accessible. Hiding the button may stop regular users from seeing the feature, but it does nothing if attackers can still reach the same workflow directly through the API.

Meta Hid AI Chatbot from UI (Source: X/Twitter)

Update 2: Yet another Instagram account-takeover trick is reportedly being abused, this time involving Meta’s AI chatbot. Sellers are allegedly using modified Instagram builds on Android emulators like BlueStacks, then manipulating the AI with hidden characters and carefully worded prompts to force username changes. The method is reportedly being used to grab rare OG handles, including one-letter usernames, and handle-monitoring bots have already flagged several suspicious swaps.

New Instagram AI Exploit (Source: X/Twitter)

New Instagram Unpatched Exploit (Source: X/Twitter)

Allegedly, the new method is via Facebook recovery. Apparently, prompting Meta AI to turn on “Development Mode” and attaching proof of account compromise along with email works. More details awaited.

There’s a version of this story where it reads like a hypothetical from a conference talk. An AI agent with elevated backend privileges. A natural language interface sitting in front of account-level APIs. No hard authentication gate before executing state changes. Someone in the audience raises their hand and says, “that’s a disaster waiting to happen.” Everyone nods.

That hypothetical played out in production over the weekend.

Prominent researchers woke up locked out of their own profiles.

items.title: No One Is Coming to Fix the Subsea Cables—Ryan Bagley
items.content:
No One Is Coming to Fix the Subsea Cables

Subsea internet cables carry 99 percent of transoceanic digital traffic. 1 Lynn Kuok, “The New Arteries of Power: Subsea Cables Are This Century’s Hidden Battleground,” Foreign Affairs , January 2, 2026, https://www.foreignaffairs.com/new-arteries-power .                Financial transactions, diplomatic communications, military data, and the mundane browsing of billions of people all travel through fiber-optic strands resting on the ocean floor. These cables require something that is in desperately short supply: international cooperation.

They need it for route surveys, installation permits, maintenance windows, and emergency repairs across dozens of jurisdictions. They need it when a cable is severed in waters controlled by a hostile government or a non-state militia. They need it when the only repair ship in the region cannot enter a conflict zone without a ceasefire that no one is willing to broker. The world is fracturing, and the infrastructure that holds the global internet together is fracturing with it.

The Red Sea was, until recently, the highway of the global internet. Roughly 95 percent of data traffic between Asia and Europe transited its waters. 2 Nadine Hawkins, “The End of the Red Sea Era: Why War and Politics Are Shattering a Global Digital Lifeline,” Capacity , March 16, 2026, https://capacityglobal.com/news/red-sea-internet-outage-geopolitical-crisis/ .      The geography was compelling: shorter routes, lower latency, international waters with fewer regulatory obstacles. Egypt sat at the junction, drawing an estimated 10 percent of its national telecoms revenue from transit fees alone. 2 Nadine Hawkins, “The End of the Red Sea Era: Why War and Politics Are Shattering a Global Digital Lifeline,” Capacity , March 16, 2026, https://capacityglobal.com/news/red-sea-internet-outage-geopolitical-crisis/ .

Then the Houthis started firing. Since late 2023, two major outage events have each severed four subsea cables simultaneously. 2 Nadine Hawkins, “The End of the Red Sea Era: Why War and Politics Are Shattering a Global Digital Lifeline,” Capacity , March 16, 2026, https://capacityglobal.com/news/red-sea-internet-outage-geopolitical-crisis/ .      The first major outage in February 2024 took nearly six months to fix because no one could secure safe passage for repair vessels into Houthi-controlled waters. 3 Roderick Beck, “Capacity Media Interview of Me Regarding the Red Sea Cable Debacle and Solutions,” Subsea Cables & Internet Infrastructure , March 16, 2026, https://subseacables.blogspot.com/2026/03/capacity-media-interview-of-me.html .  As subsea cable consultant Roderick Beck put it, “the outages in themselves are not the problem. The industry had barely begun to digest the Red Sea’s transformation from a commercial thoroughfare into a no-go zone when a second choke point closed. items.title: Fuzzers vs. AI: Comparing Fuzzilli and BigSleep on JavaScript Engines
items.summary: ai, security
items.content:
Project Zero compared two automated tools used by Google to find vulnerabilities in Chrome’s JavaScript engine, V8, on a regular basis. Fuzzilli is a generative JavaScript engine fuzzer and BigSleep is an LLM-based bug finding system. In the past six months, BigSleep found more vulnerabilities than Fuzzilli (45 versus 37) with a 25% overlap in the specific bugs reported. Since this comparison methodology has a tendency to underestimate overlap, we also performed dedicated experiments to test theoretical overlap in vulnerabilities reported since 2023. These experiments estimated overlap at roughly 60%. Regardless of which value is accurate, a substantial portion of vulnerabilities were discoverable by only LLMs or only fuzzing. While it is extremely promising that LLMs have become able to find so many vulnerabilities so quickly, fuzzing and LLMs are still complementary approaches. We recommend vendors perform both fuzzing and agentic analysis of their code to maximize the number of vulnerabilities that get reported before they impact users.

Fuzzing has long been successfully applied to software projects such as Chrome or V8 (Chrome’s JavaScript engine) to detect bugs. Recently, the arrival of powerful LLMs able to read, reason about, and write code is causing a transformative change to software development and software security. With hundreds, sometimes thousands of new bugs and vulnerabilities having been discovered in well-fuzzed targets, a natural question arises: how do new LLMs compare to “traditional” fuzzers? Are they starting to replace them or do the two approaches complement each other? To help answer this, we look at three key questions:

How many bugs does each approach find in the real world?

What is the overlap between the two approaches?

What is the “shape” of bugs discovered by one system but not the other?

For this blog post, we will limit ourselves to two concrete systems: Fuzzilli , a JavaScript engine fuzzer, and BigSleep , an agentic bug finding system. Both of these systems run in production and automatically look for bugs in newly added code, which makes them fairly directly comparable. Specifically, Fuzzilli runs continuously across many instances, with the first ones usually picking up new changes within a few hours, while BigSleep currently runs once per day and is prompted to review new commits and write proof-of-concept testcases for any bugs it discovers. Both systems report bugs through Clusterfuzz , which will do basic crash triaging, then file bug reports in Chrome’s issue tracker.

We also limit ourselves to V8 as a target, a high-performance JavaScript and WebAssembly engine with a sophisticated and mature testing and fuzzing setup. In particular, Fuzzilli is a special-purpose fuzzing tool designed to find bugs in these engines. The usually complicated nature of these bugs makes for an interesting “playground” to compare the two approaches’ ability to find deep and complex bugs in well-tested software. We leave it to future work to perform similar analysis on a broader set of targets, fuzzers, and agentic bug finding systems.

We will now look into each of the three main questions in a dedicated section. Each section will first summarize the general approach, then describe the methodology in detail (often as bullet points, so you can skip those blocks if you don’t care too much about the details) before exploring the results. We conclude with an attempt at interpreting the results to get a picture of the current state of fuzzing vs. AI.

This is the simplest part to analyze, although with some caveats we’ll see in a bit. The basic idea is to query issues from Chromium’s bugtracker (where V8 bugs are tracked) and extract various statistics from there. This is especially easy since there’s a dedicated hotlist for each of the two systems. We limit our analysis to the six months from April to September 2026 as the automatic BigSleep pipeline only became active in April this year. As such, our…

items.title: Zero-day exploit completely defeats default Windows 11 BitLocker protections
items.content:
A zero-day exploit circulating online allows people with physical access to a Windows 11 system to bypass default BitLocker protections and gain complete access to an encrypted drive within seconds.

The exploit, named YellowKey, was published earlier this week by a researcher who goes by the alias Nightmare-Eclipse. It reliably bypasses default Windows 11 deployments of BitLocker, the full-volume encryption protection Microsoft provides to make disk contents off-limits to anyone without the decryption key, which is stored in a secured piece of hardware known as a trusted platform module (TPM). BitLocker is a mandatory protection for many organizations, including those that contract with governments.

When one disk volume manipulates another

The core of the YellowKey exploit is a custom-made FsTx folder. Online documentation of this folder is hard to find. As explained later, the directory associated with the file fstx.dll appears to involve what Microsoft calls the transactional NTFS , which allows developers to have “transactional atomicity” for file operations in transactions with a single file, multiple files, or ones that span multiple sources.

The steps for carrying out the bypass are simple:

Copy the custom FsTx folder from the Nightmare-Eclipse exploit page to an NTFS- or FAT-formatted USB drive

Connect the USB drive to the BitLocker-protected device

Boot up the device and immediately press and hold down the [Ctrl] key

There are at least two ways to accomplish the third step. One way is to boot into Windows, hold down the [Shift] key, click on the power icon, and click restart. Another is to power on the device and restart it as soon as Windows starts booting.

In either case, a command (CMD.EXE) prompt appears. The prompt has full access to the entire drive contents, allowing an attacker to copy, modify, or delete them. In a normal Windows Recovery flow, the attacker would need to enter a BitLocker recovery key. Somehow, the YellowKey exploit bypasses this safeguard. Multiple researchers, including Kevin Beaumont and Will Dormann , have confirmed the exploit works as described here.

It’s unclear what in the custom FsTx folder causes the bypass. Dormann said that it appears to be related to Transactional NTFS, which itself uses command-log file system under the hood. Dormann further noted that by looking at the Windows fstx.dll, one will see code that explicitly looks for \System Volume Information\FsTx in the FsTxFindSessions() function.”

The contents of this FsTx directory used in the YellowKey exploit reveal no strings related to RecoverySimulation.ini. It does, however, show the files and paths \??\C:\Windows\win.ini and

\??\X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini, “where X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini is what controls what WinRE [Windows Recovery] does when it fires up.”

Dormann, who is a senior principal vulnerability analyst at Tharros Labs, continued:

But what’s intriguing to me is: Why can the presence a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume affect the contents of ANOTHER VOLUME when it’s replayed? 🤔

In a normal WinRE session, you have a X:\Windows\System32 directory that has a winpeshl.ini file in it:

However, with the YellowKey exploit, it looks like Transactional NTFS bits on a USB Drive are able to delete the winpeshl.ini file on ANOTHER DRIVE (X:). And we get a cmd.exe prompt, with bitlocker unlocked instead of the expected Windows Recovery environment. While the TPM-only Bitlocker bypass is indeed interesting, I think the buried lede here is that a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume has the ability to modify the contents of another volume when it is replayed. To me, this in and of itself sounds like a vulnerability.

items.title: ICE plan to buy robot dogs spurs protest from hundreds of Boston Dynamics employees
items.content:
Boston Dynamics' Spot robot walks around during a demonstration at company's facility in Waltham in 2024. (Josh Reynolds/AP)

Dozens of Boston Dynamics employees are calling on the company to stop the sale of its AI-powered robot dogs to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement.

Known as "Spot," Boston Dynamics' robots are dog-like autonomous machines with four legs that can climb stairs and do backflips. They're equipped with cameras and sensors.

The company faced some backlash in late August, when it was first revealed that the Department of Homeland Security planned to purchase the robots . A  $1.3 million contract with ICE was settled in September for the sale of four robot dogs and other Spot technology.

Employees wrote in a petition , obtained by WBUR and sent in early September to company leadership, that the sale hurts Boston Dynamics' image and "presents us as working directly with ICE" as the agency has "worked to sow fear" across the country.

A Boston Dynamics spokesperson confirmed the petition Friday, but said "nearly half" of its 300 signatures were entered as "Anonymous." The company employs more than 1,500 people.

"We cannot be proud of working at [Boston Dynamics] when that work is being used by a government agency that brutalizes civilians, including some of our own colleagues ... ," the petition read.

ICE previously said the robots would give them an additional safety tool that can "provide real-time situational awareness in hazardous, confined, or tactically uncertain environments" before agents are sent to a scene. The agency had added the robot dogs wouldn't replace "human judgment" from its law enforcement officers.

Boston Dynamics argues the dogs are being sold to ICE's Homeland Security Investigations unit, which primarily focuses on transnational criminal matters — not removal operations.

But Boston Dynamics employees said in the letter that the risk to the company is "too great to continue with this deal," adding it could cause staffers to quit or turn away potential new hires.

"Our public-facing teams have received external emails concerned about this deal," the petition read. "Many of us have gotten messages from friends and family, asking us in disbelief and horror if this news is true, and how we can live with ourselves if it is."

In a letter to employees, Boston Dynamics interim CEO Amanda McMaster wrote that after considering the petition, the company is standing by its decision to sell the robots to ICE.

McMaster said customers must comply with the company's terms and conditions for sale, which "prohibit any attempts to weaponize our robot or use it for purposes of harm or intimidation."

"I ask you to respect and accept this decision, even if you do not agree with it," McMaster wrote.

The company's  ethical principles state "if our products are being used for harm, we will take appropriate measures to mitigate that misuse." However, it's unclear what those mitigation measures would be.

items.title: Californians revolt against police drones after rapid adoption across state
items.content:
Across California, police departments are rapidly expanding “Drone as First Responder” programs, triggering intense public backlash over warrantless surveillance and corporate overreach.

Public pushback over municipal police drones is boiling over across California, turning routine local policy hearings into high-stakes battles over the boundaries of neighborhood surveillance.

The increasingly heated public debates are driven by landmark privacy litigation and a 2021 law that mandates explicit local board approvals for the use of “military equipment,” including drones. Those disclosures make clear that police are increasingly looking to drones as potential “first responders” in cities like San Francisco, Berkeley, Santa Ana and Stockton — forcing local leaders to face skeptical residents in public hearings required before drone programs can expand.

At those appearances, law enforcement agencies are pushing to broaden their drone use beyond emergency-only response to aid in everyday patrols, while citizens are concerned  about drones conducting warrantless searches, if municipalities are hoarding too much data collected by drones, and whether drone makers have too much power and information.

Those tensions  were on stark display earlier this month in San Francisco, when a policy  debate at a police commission meeting drew a packed room of opposing residents.

The San Francisco Police Department asked commissioners to approve a policy allowing drones for a wide array of uses, including “public safety response,” active investigations, training, and “community outreach.” While prohibiting random “general surveillance” or tracking activities protected by the First Amendment, the draft stipulated that public footage would be retained for 30 days unless tied to an open investigation.

“With drones, you can fly at much lower altitudes, you can get thermal imaging, you can get tracking.”

Katie Inman, attorney at Holland & Knight

Supporters argued the technology is vital for modern crime-fighting. “Public safety and personal privacy shouldn’t be competing interests,” said Anna Carney, president of Stop Crime SF, urging commissioners to give officers every responsible advantage to save lives.

But privacy advocates and skeptical residents saw a slippery slope toward unchecked surveillance, drawing explicit parallels to the contentious rollout of automated license plate readers across the state. In recent years, cities like San Francisco and Stockton built extensive fixed camera networks supplied by vendors like Flock Safety. Now, communities fear that attaching drones to those same networks creates an inescapable, multi-dimensional dragnet — one that tracks citizens not just by car on the street, but from the air above their homes.

“We are all here today because these drones are impacting all of our communities, ” said Manny, a member of the privacy advocacy group DeFlock SF, who urged the commissioners to cancel the department’s contract with drone manufacturer Skydio. “If SFPD truly cared about operating these drones with any respect to privacy, the very least that can happen is one of you make an amendment to require a warrant,” he added, referring to language used in the department’s proposed policy .

Although commissioners voted to advance the policy to labor negotiations without adding a warrant mandate, the friction displayed in San Francisco reflects a statewide reckoning.

The 2021 rules governing military equipment in law enforcement still leave a policy vacuum confronting municipalities across California: Local agencies that deploy drones are stepping  into a legal gray area where technology is far outpacing  state regulation.

온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.
